decisions.because: Counterexample R5-F1 on c51cdc9: node 3 replayed the handshake node 2 had sent it to node 1, which authenticated node 3's connection as node 2 and sent node 1's broadcasts for node 2 to node 3. A recipient/nonce in the handshake would not stop a live two-way relay; the WireGuard tunnel address is authenticated by the peer's tunnel key (ADR-0027, owner chose B on 2026-10-12).

statement: A pinned node that the peers file binds to an address authenticates only on a connection from that address: a handshake from any other source is refused and counted (sokol_mesh_handshakes_wrong_address_total), so another peer cannot relay its handshake and take over delivery to it; a reload that binds it elsewhere closes its connection on its next envelope. One address cannot be bound to two nodes. A node bound to no address is accepted from any address and named at startup.
